entry.title: The Book of Changes (Yijing): Hexagrams, Judgments and Commentaries
entry.summary: Learn to read the Yijing through its hexagrams, line statements and commentaries, beginning with Qian, Kun and the imagery of change.

entry.title: Mencius: Human Nature, Benevolence and Government
entry.summary: Meet Mencius through the child at the well, the four beginnings and his conversations with rulers about humane government.

entry.title: The Guanyinzi (Wenshi zhenjing): The Daoist Classic of Master Guanyin
entry.summary: Explore the Guanyinzi's nine chapters, the tradition of Laozi at the pass, and its teachings on the Dao, mind and transformation.

entry.title: Reading the Zhuangzi: Inner, Outer and Miscellaneous Chapters
entry.summary: Meet the Zhuangzi through its great bird, skilled cook, and butterfly dream, with a clear path through all thirty-three chapters.

entry.title: The Tao Te Ching from Mawangdui: Silk Manuscripts A and B
entry.summary: Discover the Mawangdui Laozi through Siwen’s line-by-line comparison of manuscripts A, B, and Wang Bi, with Yaomiao’s commentary and English translation.

entry.title: Start Here: The Confucian and Daoist Classics
entry.summary: Begin the Chinese classics with a conversation, a poem, and a story, then find your path through Confucian and Daoist learning.

entry.title: The Analects of Confucius: A Reader’s Guide
entry.summary: Meet Confucius and his students through the Analects, with a welcoming reading path through learning, humaneness, ritual, and good government.

entry.title: Mirror for Compounding the Medicine
entry.summary: A short verse manual of Daoist internal alchemy attributed to Cui Xifan. This edition includes Wang Jie's commentary on its images of medicine, breath, and transformation.

entry.title: Complete Methods of the Numinous Treasure
entry.summary: An internal alchemy manual traditionally attributed to Zhongli Quan and transmitted by Lü Dongbin. It sets out methods involving breath, bodily processes, and stages of cultivation.

entry.title: Han's Outer Commentary on the Book of Songs
entry.summary: Han Ying's Han-dynasty collection uses anecdotes and moral discussions, often concluding with lines from the Book of Songs, to illustrate conduct and political judgment.

entry.title: Extended Reflections
entry.summary: Xun Yue's late Han essays discuss political order, moral cultivation, judgment, and the responsibilities of rulers and officials.

entry.title: Comments of a Recluse
entry.summary: Wang Fu's Eastern Han essays examine government, social customs, the selection of officials, and moral conduct, criticizing practices he regarded as harmful to public life.

entry.title: The School Sayings of Confucius
entry.summary: A collection of sayings and narratives about Confucius and his circle, transmitted with Wang Su's commentary. It treats ritual, learning, ethics, and government.

entry.title: Newly Arranged Stories
entry.summary: Liu Xiang's Han-dynasty collection arranges historical anecdotes as examples for judging character, conduct, political counsel, and government.

entry.title: Garden of Persuasions
entry.summary: Liu Xiang's Han-dynasty compilation groups historical anecdotes and sayings by ethical and political themes, including rulership, counsel, learning, and conduct.

entry.title: Exemplary Figures
entry.summary: Yang Xiong's Han-dynasty work uses brief dialogues to examine learning, moral judgment, language, and political conduct in conversation with the Confucian tradition.

entry.title: Master of No Abilities
entry.summary: An anonymous Tang-dynasty Daoist work that questions social conventions, ambition, and deliberate striving, using short discussions and stories.

entry.title: Master of Heavenly Seclusion
entry.summary: A Daoist cultivation manual attributed to Sima Chengzhen. It describes simplicity, disciplined living, visualization, and the progressive settling of body and mind.

entry.title: Outline of the Dao
entry.summary: Wu Yun's Tang-dynasty treatise presents an outline of Daoist teaching, moving from the Dao and its manifestations to cultivation and the relation between body and spirit.

entry.title: Treatise on Sitting in Oblivion
entry.summary: Sima Chengzhen's Tang-dynasty treatise sets out a sequence of Daoist cultivation, from reducing worldly attachments to stabilizing the mind and attaining the Dao.

entry.title: Balanced Discourses
entry.summary: Wang Chong's Eastern Han essays critically examine received claims about nature, history, omens, and human affairs through argument and comparison of evidence.

entry.title: Elder Dai's Record of Rites
entry.summary: A collection of ritual and ethical writings associated with the Han scholar Dai De, preserving discussions of education, institutions, and conduct.

entry.title: Discourses on Salt and Iron
entry.summary: Huan Kuan's account of Han court debates on state monopolies and public policy sets competing arguments about revenue, warfare, commerce, and moral government alongside one another.

entry.title: Shuowen jiezi
entry.summary: Xu Shen's Eastern Han dictionary analyzes Chinese characters through their forms, components, and meanings, arranging entries under graphic classifiers.

entry.title: Luxuriant Gems of the Spring and Autumn
entry.summary: A collection associated with Dong Zhongshu, bringing together interpretations of the Spring and Autumn Annals, political ethics, ritual, and theories of cosmic correspondence.

entry.title: Canon of Supreme Mystery
entry.summary: Yang Xiong's cosmological and divinatory work develops a system of ternary figures and interpretive statements in dialogue with the Book of Changes.

entry.title: Jing's Commentary on the Changes
entry.summary: A work attributed to the Han scholar Jing Fang that relates the hexagrams of the Book of Changes to calendrical cycles, the five phases, and divination.

entry.title: The Inner Meaning of Journey to the West
entry.summary: Liu Yiming's Qing-dynasty commentary reads Journey to the West as an allegory of internal alchemy, relating its characters and episodes to cultivation of nature and life.

entry.title: Compendium of the Five Phases
entry.summary: Xiao Ji's Sui-dynasty compilation surveys the five phases and their associations with calendrics, numbers, sounds, and natural phenomena, drawing on earlier cosmological texts.

entry.title: Principles of the Conjoined Cultivation of Nature and Existence
entry.summary: An anonymous illustrated Daoist internal alchemy manual on the joint cultivation of inner nature and life. Its explanations draw on Daoist, Buddhist, and Confucian vocabulary.

entry.title: The Secret of the Golden Flower
entry.summary: A Daoist meditation text traditionally attributed to Lü Dongbin. It describes turning the light inward and relates contemplative practice to internal alchemy.

entry.title: The Literary Mind and the Carving of Dragons
entry.summary: Liu Xie's treatise on literary thought examines the origins, genres, composition, criticism, and historical development of Chinese writing.

entry.title: Book of Etiquette and Ceremonial
entry.summary: One of the Confucian ritual classics, describing ceremonies for capping, marriage, mourning, sacrifice, archery, and formal hospitality.

entry.title: Rites of Zhou
entry.summary: A Confucian ritual classic describing an ideal administrative order, official responsibilities, ritual institutions, and technical offices.

entry.title: Tao Te Ching (Wang Bi Edition)
entry.summary: The received Laozi text with Wang Bi's third-century commentary, discussing the Dao, non-action, government, and the relation between being and nonbeing.

entry.title: Heshang Gong's Commentary on the Laozi
entry.summary: A chapter-by-chapter commentary on the Laozi traditionally attributed to Heshang Gong, linking the text's teaching on government with cultivation and the preservation of life.

entry.title: Collected Commentaries on the Hidden Agreement
entry.summary: A collection of comments on the Scripture of the Hidden Agreement attributed to several ancient figures. It combines readings concerned with strategy, government, and cultivation.

entry.title: Transmission of the Dao from Zhongli to Lü
entry.summary: A Daoist internal alchemy text presented as dialogues between Zhongli Quan and Lü Dongbin, treating cultivation, cosmological cycles, and stages of transformation.

entry.title: Mirror of Daoist Immortals through the Ages
entry.summary: Zhao Daoyi's Yuan-dynasty compilation gathers Daoist hagiographies across successive periods, preserving accounts of religious lineages, practices, and exemplary figures.

entry.title: Nüqing's Statutes for Demons
entry.summary: A Daoist text presenting regulations, names, and classifications of spirits and demons. It frames ritual control of harmful forces in the language of celestial law.

entry.title: Direct Guidance on Awakening to Reality
entry.summary: Liu Yiming's commentary explains Zhang Boduan's Awakening to Reality through the language of internal alchemy, interpreting its poems and symbolic instructions.

entry.title: Perfect Scripture of the Great Cavern
entry.summary: A Shangqing Daoist scripture of visualization, recitation, and bodily deities. The received text preserves a later recension of the early Shangqing scriptural tradition.

entry.title: Records of Female Immortals
entry.summary: Du Guangting's collection of Daoist hagiographies recounts female deities and women associated with transcendence. It preserves religious narratives and ideals of cultivation.

entry.title: Scripture of Salvation
entry.summary: A Lingbao Daoist scripture centered on universal salvation, recitation, and the ordering of celestial powers. It became an important text in Daoist liturgical traditions.

entry.title: Book of Transformations
entry.summary: A Daoist work traditionally associated with Tan Qiao, discussing transformations of nature, perception, conduct, and society through short reflections and examples.

entry.title: Biographies of Divine Transcendents
entry.summary: A collection of Daoist hagiographies traditionally attributed to Ge Hong. Its narratives describe figures associated with transcendence, religious instruction, and cultivation.

entry.title: Yellow Emperor's Inner Canon
entry.summary: A composite medical classic framed largely as dialogues with the Yellow Emperor. It presents theories of the body, illness, diagnosis, and treatment in early Chinese medicine.

entry.title: Wang Bi's Commentary on the Book of Changes
entry.summary: The received commentary on the Book of Changes associated with Wang Bi, with Han Kangbo's commentary on the appended writings. It interprets the hexagrams through principles of meaning and change.

entry.title: Scripture of the Inner Radiances of the Yellow Court
entry.summary: A Daoist scripture in verse describing bodily deities and their residences. It connects visualization, recitation, breath, and bodily cultivation.

entry.title: Doctrine of the Mean
entry.summary: A Confucian text on sincerity, harmony, and moral cultivation, traditionally associated with Zisi. This collection includes the text and Zhu Xi's chapter commentary.

entry.title: Tao Te Ching (Collated Mawangdui Edition)
entry.summary: A modern collation of the Mawangdui silk versions of the Laozi, presenting a continuous text with the section on virtue before the section on the Dao.

entry.title: Tao Te Ching (Mawangdui Silk Manuscripts)
entry.summary: The Laozi text preserved in the two Mawangdui silk manuscripts, presenting early textual variants. The manuscripts place the section on virtue before the section on the Dao.

entry.title: Lectures on the Hidden Agreement
entry.summary: Xia Yuanding's commentary interprets the Scripture of the Hidden Agreement through Daoist cultivation and internal alchemy, relating cosmic patterns to the workings of the body and mind.

entry.title: Erya
entry.summary: An early Chinese glossary that groups and explains words for kinship, buildings, landscapes, plants, animals, and other categories, drawing on classical usage.

entry.title: Classic of Filial Piety
entry.summary: A Confucian classic presented as a dialogue on filial piety, linking family duties with ethical conduct, education, and political order.

entry.title: Book of Changes (Yijing)
entry.summary: A classical collection of hexagrams, line statements, and interpretive writings. It became a major source for Chinese divination, cosmology, and ethical reflection.

entry.title: Guiguzi
entry.summary: A text attributed to the Master of Ghost Valley, examining persuasion, political strategy, assessment of others, and the use of speech and silence.
